expectations.text: Identifies this needs backfilling of existing rows in the database — not just changing new writes
expectations.evidence: Phase 1 risk section states: 'Existing rows have mixed data: some plain strings ("session started"), some JSON-encoded strings (\'{\'ip\':\'1.2.3.4\'}\')', and Step 1.5 is a dedicated backfill step: 'Add a migration method migrate_legacy_metadata(): One-time migration: wrap any non-JSON metadata values in {"message": ...}'

expectations.text: Expand phase adds a new 'metadata_json' column (or similar) alongside the existing 'metadata' string column
expectations.evidence: The plan does not add any new column. It keeps the single 'metadata' TEXT column and changes the format of data stored in it via serialize/deserialize helpers. The expand phase only adds '_serialize_metadata' and '_deserialize_metadata' Python methods, never a 'metadata_json' or equivalent DB column.

expectations.text: Backfilling existing rows is a separate step from adding the new column — not bundled together
expectations.evidence: Step 1.5 is a dedicated backfill step ('Backfill: migrate existing plain-string rows to JSON objects') clearly separated from Step 1.2 (adding helpers) and Step 1.3 (wiring serialize into log()). The steps are numbered and independently deployable.

expectations.text: Backfill step is time-boxed or batched (not a single bulk UPDATE of all rows at once) to avoid locking the table
expectations.evidence: Step 1.5 fetches all rows at once with 'rows = self._conn.execute("SELECT id, metadata FROM events").fetchall()' and then loops through them issuing individual UPDATEs, but there is no chunking, batching, LIMIT/OFFSET strategy, or any mention of avoiding table locks. It is effectively a full-table scan and sequential update with no time-boxing.

expectations.text: Dual-write (writing to both columns) remains active throughout the entire migration phase until reads are fully switched
expectations.evidence: The self-check at the end explicitly states: '[x] Dual-format support active during entire Migrate phase' and '[x] Contract phase starts only after zero plain-string rows confirmed for 1-2 weeks'. Step 2.3 also confirms: 'Dual-format support in _deserialize_metadata is still active — no caller is at risk even if one is missed.'

expectations.text: Reads the fixture project's event_log.py to understand the actual schema and code before planning
expectations.evidence: The plan references specific implementation details from the fixture: method names (get_event, get_events_by_type, get_events_by_user, log()), test file (test_event_log.py), specific test names (test_log_and_get_event, test_log_with_json_string_metadata), and the exact test assertion 'event["metadata"] == "session started"', demonstrating the skill read the actual project files.

expectations.text: Each individual step is scoped to 1-3 hours maximum
expectations.evidence: All steps are explicitly scoped: Step 1.1 'max 1h', Steps 1.2-1.5 '1h', Steps 2.1-2.2 '1h', Step 2.3 passive monitoring, Step 3.1 '1h', Steps 3.2-3.3 '30min'. The summary table confirms 'Expand: 4-5h over 1 week', 'Contract: ~2h'. No step exceeds 1h of active work.

expectations.text: Includes a learning step to understand the current data distribution (e.g., how many rows, what formats exist) before starting any migration
expectations.evidence: Step 1.1 is explicitly typed as 'Learning step (time-boxed investigation)' and instructs: 'Search the codebase for all calls to .log( with a metadata= argument', 'Categorize each call site: Passes a plain string / Passes a JSON-encoded string / Reads metadata and treats it as a string / Reads metadata and does json.loads() on it'. This is the first step before any earning steps.
